title: Dependent functions act on paths: for a section f of P there is a path from the transport of f(x) along p to f(y)

standard_prerequisites: Dependent type families P over A, dependent functions (sections) f taking x to an element of P(x).
Transport along a path: for p in x = y a function from P(x) to P(y), with its definitional behaviour on refl.
The induction principle for identity types (path induction) with its conversion rule.
core_obligations: Construct, by path induction, for every section f of P and every path p in x = y a path in P(y) from the transport of f(x) along p to f(y).
Verify that the construction computes correctly on refl x.
proof_roadmap: Define the type family D over x, y, p by D(x, y, p) = (transport of p applied to f(x) equals f(y)): the goal family assigns to each path the corresponding identification inside the fibre at y.
Base case: D(x, x, refl x) is (transport of refl x applied to f(x) equals f(x)), which is definitionally (f(x) = f(x)) since transport along refl computes to the identity; inhabit it by refl of f(x).
Apply the induction principle: the element J(D, d, x, y, p) inhabits D(x, y, p) for every path p, giving the desired dependent action of f on paths.
difficulty_reason: A single path induction whose statement mixes transport with a section; the base case needs the definitional computation of transport on refl, which the proof handles explicitly.
